chunk-001:c001.proposition: Compatibilism should identify the important notions of freedom and willing that survive determinism rather than claim to preserve the libertarian conception unchanged.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley states this as his governing positive conception of compatibilism, so it independently establishes the standard his side defends without requiring an earlier opposing move.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: On monism or physicalism, a person's brain states are parts of that person, so neural causation does not displace personal agency or establish that the person was not the source.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley's monist identification of brain states as parts of the embodied person supplies a freestanding account of personal-level causation even if no earlier neural-displacement objection is retained.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Even if willing is determined, morally important distinctions between willing and unwilling conduct, including consent, survive and provide substantive content for compatibilist freedom.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley affirmatively grounds compatibilist agency in the surviving distinctions between consent, willing, and unwilling conduct, making the proposition independently constructive.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: A decision produced by weighted stochastic variation may remain no better than randomness for purposes of authorship when the agent's weighting criteria constrain the possible result.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley's reconstruction directly identifies a general limitation of criteria-weighted stochastic choice: probabilistic variation alone does not establish the unrestricted authorship at issue.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Genetics and upbringing heavily constrain an agent's evaluative criteria and place much of the possible choice space outside the agent's control, challenging claims of ultimate sourcehood.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley independently traces evaluative criteria to inherited and environmental influences, establishing a substantive formative constraint on ultimate authorship without relying on an earlier retained reply target.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: A libertarian model may not deliver the ultimate responsibility commonly expected of it when a restrictive environment prevents an agent from developing access to materially different evaluative criteria.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley's isolated-agent example independently exposes the responsibility consequences of an externally restricted evaluative outlook, so the proposition can function as a constructive constraint on responsibility theories.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Under determinism, compatibilism should reconstruct freedom around practically useful distinctions such as chosen versus unchosen action instead of asserting that traditional libertarian freedom survives intact.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley presents the chosen-versus-unchosen distinction as a positive account of what freedom and will should preserve in a deterministic world, so it stands without opposition.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: An alternatives-based account needs a principled way to determine when an option was genuinely live, particularly in cases where restrictive upbringing appears to exclude alternative evaluative paths.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley's Jojo discussion independently establishes the need for an operational live-option criterion before alternative possibilities can explain deliberation and responsibility across constrained cases.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: A determined agent can remain the proximal cause of later conduct because causally formed character and deliberation operate within closed causal processes and explain the agent's behavior.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley positively identifies causally effective character and proximal causation as a sufficient nonultimate form of sourcehood, yielding a freestanding compatibilist account if the preferred reply is orphaned.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Freedom and responsibility comprise plural, practice-shaped concepts whose content can be reconstructed through praise, blame, coercion, and reactive attitudes rather than one metaphysical formula.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley's pragmatic account independently grounds responsibility in the purposes and structure of actual reactive-attitude practices, so it remains constructive without an earlier libertarian formula to answer.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: If agents cannot deliberate from the first-person perspective without treating themselves as able to do otherwise, that ineliminable experience poses a serious unresolved challenge for deterministic compatibilism.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley expressly acknowledges this internal pressure on his view; as a constructive fallback, it independently identifies a burden any adequate compatibilist theory of deliberation must satisfy.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Even if determinism were proven, distinctions between choices and nonchoices could remain intelligible, while tension between objective inquiry and first-person deliberation would burden theories of human inquiry generally.

orphanFallback.rationale: Folley directly offers the surviving choice distinction and generalizes the reflexive inquiry problem, providing a positive compatibilist treatment that does not depend on an earlier retained objection.
